spans.text: The light that stays after the sun
Layout is a sentence, not a shape
Every scene in Soundstage is laid out by the rules a designer already knows:
, minimum and maximum widths, and constraints against a reference size.
This span is larger, italic and blue.
Paragraph spacing separates paragraphs, and the first line of this one is indented by thirty-two pixels, the way a printed book would set it. The rest of the paragraph wraps back to the margin.
Hug sizes a frame to its content.
Fill shares the free space equally, freezing at min and max.
Fixed keeps the size you set.
The rows below exercise wrapping, fill, baselines and rotation.

A card row: fill children with min and max widths
This card fills its share of the row and never shrinks below 220 pixels.
This one fills too, but freezes at 320 pixels; the others take what it leaves.
Each image fills its frame and keeps its focal point in view as the card resizes.
